# ADR 0001 — Factored-attention kernel

**Status: OPEN — awaiting owner acceptance.** Lane L4, 2026-09-11. Every number is regenerated by
`docs/adr/0001-cost-model.py` (stdlib only).

## 1. Context

The gist tracker factors **pre-RoPE** keys, so a stored key is `K_t = R_t U c_t` with a per-token
rotation `R_t`; rotation does not commute with the projection, so `q·K_t != (Uᵀq)·c_t`. So
`_ensure_mid_cache` (`src/kvdlra/cache/bug_cache.py`) reconstructs the whole n-dim middle (fp32 U·C, re-rotated at true positions, cast to bf16) and `_decode_peek` concatenates `[sinks | exact tier
| gist | recent]` into a dense `n x T` array attention reads every step: Theta(T) tokens attended in
n dims, so the storage ratio never reaches memory or throughput. Measured on Llama-3.1-8B,
A100-40GB, batch 1 (`results/w20-close-report.md` §2), the r64 configuration (`bugSseed-r64-h256`)
runs **103 / 188 / 508 ms per token** at **KV peak 3.25 / 6.45 / 12.83 GB** for 16K / 32K / 64K,
against full KV at **26 / 28 / 37 ms, 2.05 / 4.08 / 8.14 GB** and KIVI-2 at **44 / 68 / 119 ms, 0.45
/ 0.89 / 1.78 GB**. At 32K the stored state is 0.56 GB: ~91 % of that peak is workspace.

## 2. Decision drivers

Gate 3 pass criteria, `docs/plan/ICML2027_PLAN.md` §2 (one bracket replaces a word `CLAUDE.md`
bans):

> *Pass for Branch A:* [r64-configuration] kernel resident KV ≤ 0.25× full at 32K
> and decode tokens/s ≥ full KV at 64K, batch ≥4. If it lands at ≥ full-KV
> throughput but not below, Branch A still works on the memory axis alone (that
> lets you fit batch 8 where full KV fits batch 2 — measure that).

Week-3 kernel gate, verbatim from `docs/plan/lanes/L4_kernel.md`:

> Gate: kernel KV peak < full KV at 32K and ms/token < reconstruct path by ≥ 3×.

Two further constraints: Week-12 attributed retrieval to the exact tier *under the pre-RoPE basis*,
so changing the basis re-opens an accuracy question; and `lazy_initialization` raises above batch 1,
so batch ≥ 4 needs a batched cache before Gate 3 can be read.

## 3. Options

Shapes: L = 32 layers, H_q = 32 query heads, H_kv = 8 KV heads, D = 128, n = H_kv·D = 1024, GQA
group G = H_q/H_kv = 4, r ∈ {64, 128}. The r64 configuration keeps 4 verbatim sinks, an exact tier
of 256, a recent ring at high water 47, absorb block 16; T_mid = T − 307 low-rank columns. U (n×r)
and C (r×T_mid) are fp32 at rest, shared across all KV heads of a layer.

### (i) Post-RoPE tracking at higher rank

Track rotated keys, `K_t ≈ U c_t`. For query head h on KV head kv(h), `q_h·K_t = (U[kv(h)]ᵀ
q_h)·c_t` — project the query once per step (`2·H_q·D·r` FLOPs), then scores are an r×T_mid GEMV per
query head and the output lifts the same way, `o_h = U_v[kv(h)] (C_v p)`. Nothing n-dim is formed;
RoPE leaves decode entirely. Per low-rank token, per layer, per sequence: **4·H_q·r FLOPs** (8,192
at r=64), `2·r·b_C` B.

### (ii) RoPE-pair-factored pre-RoPE kernel

RoPE acts on 2-D pairs. For pair j (angle θ_j) let `q_{h,j}` be the query's 2-vector, `U_{h,j}` the
2×r row block of U, `G(θ)` the 2×2 rotation, and `q̃_{h,j} = (q₂, −q₁)`. Since `G(θ)ᵀ q = cos θ·q +
sin θ·q̃`,

```
q_h · R_t U c_t = Σ_j  [cos θ_j t, sin θ_j t] · ( Q_{h,j}ᵀ U_{h,j} c_t ),
                        Q_{h,j} = [ q_{h,j} , q̃_{h,j} ] ∈ R^(2x2)
```

**Shared across tokens:** `A_{h,j} = Q_{h,j}ᵀ U_{h,j} ∈ R^(2xr)`, one per (query head, pair) —
`H_q·D·r` entries (262,144 at r=64, 512 KB bf16) built once per layer per step for `4·H_q·D·r ≈
1.05` MFLOP, independent of T. **Per token:** one 2×r matvec per (head, pair) plus the `[cos, sin]`
dot, `H_q·(D/2)·(4r+2) = 2·H_q·D·r + H_q·D`; values carry no rotation and go through coordinate
space as in (i). Total **532,480 FLOPs/token** at r=64 — exactly `G = 4×` option (iii)'s key side,
because (ii) pays `2·H_q·D·r` where reconstruction pays `2·n·r = 2·H_kv·D·r`: the shared basis is
rebuilt once per KV head and reused by all 4 query heads of the group. The two coincide under MHA;
GQA 4:1 makes reconstruction strictly cheaper.

### (iii) Triton tile-wise reconstruct inside attention

Per tile of M tokens, materialize `K̂ = U_k C_k[:,tile]` and `V̂ = U_v C_v[:,tile]` in SRAM (bf16
in, fp32 accumulate), apply RoPE at the tile's true positions, fuse QKᵀ/softmax/PV, discard. Per
low-rank token, per layer, per sequence: **4·n·r + 3n + 4·H_q·D = 281,600 FLOPs** at r=64 and the
same `2·r·b_C + 4` bytes as (i)/(ii); the `+4` is the int32 true position, already stored
(`mid_pos`) and already billed by `accounting.bug_footprint`.

### Cost model

Constants: bf16 = 2 B, fp32 = 4 B, U and C fp32 at rest (today); A100-40GB HBM 1.555 TB/s (spec,
inside the 1.5–2.0 TB/s band) and 312 TFLOP/s bf16 dense; H100-SXM 3.35 TB/s and 990 TFLOP/s;
weights 8.03 G params bf16 = 16.06 GB, read once per step for the whole batch. **Memory convention:
resident KV = stored gist + tiers**, billed exactly as `accounting.bug_footprint(...).stored_bits()`
(fp32 U and C at 32 bits, verbatim sinks/ring/tier at 16, aux words at 32), **plus transient
workspace** where an arm has one — none for the factored options beyond SRAM tiles and the output;
for the reconstruct path, the memoized bf16 `n x T` middle plus one layer's fp32 rebuild buffers.
The script's self-check pins the footprint to the published 0.151× / 0.086× at 16K r64 and full-KV
resident to the measured 4.08 GiB at 32K.

Per low-rank token, per layer, per sequence:

| arm | FLOPs/token | HBM read B/token | HBM write B/token |
|---|---|---|---|
| full KV | 16,384 | 4,096 | 0 |
| reconstruct r64 (current) | 32,960 | 11,552 | 4,096 |
| (i) r64 (r128: exactly 2x) | 8,192 | 512 | 0 |
| (ii) r64 | 532,480 | 516 | 0 |
| (iii) r64 | 281,600 | 516 | 0 |
| (iii) r128 | 543,744 | 1,028 | 0 |

The reconstruct row amortizes its rebuild over the 16-token absorb block but re-assembles
`[sinks|tier|gist|recent]` with `torch.cat` every step and attention reads it again — 3 passes over
an `n x T` bf16 array, K and V — so it is FLOP-cheap and traffic-expensive. GFLOP per decode step,
whole model, batch 1 — every column scales exactly with B, so batch 8 is 8× (e.g. (iii) r64 at 64K =
4703.6 GFLOP, (i) r64 = 138.1, full = 274.9):

| T | B | full | recon r64 | (i) r64 | (i) r128 | (ii) r64 | (iii) r64 | (iii) r128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16K | 1 | 8.6 | 17.1 | 4.4 | 8.6 | 274.1 | 145.0 | 279.9 |
| 32K | 1 | 17.2 | 34.4 | 8.7 | 17.2 | 553.3 | 292.7 | 565.0 |
| 64K | 1 | 34.4 | 69.0 | 17.3 | 34.4 | 1111.6 | 588.0 | 1135.1 |
| 128K | 1 | 68.7 | 138.1 | 34.4 | 68.7 | 2228.3 | 1178.5 | 2275.4 |

KV HBM GB per decode step (read + write; the 16.06 GB weight read is identical for every arm and
excluded) and resident KV GB. **(i), (ii) and (iii) are byte-identical** — all read U once per
layer, stream C, read the dense tiers — and store the same state, so both metrics collapse to one
column pair per rank; they differ only in FLOPs. Writes are zero except on the reconstruct path.

| T | B | HBM full | HBM recon | HBM fact r64 | HBM fact r128 | res full | res recon | res fact r64 | res fact r128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16K | 1 | 2.15 | 8.11 | 0.32 | 0.60 | 2.15 | 2.67 | 0.32 | 0.60 |
| 16K | 8 | 17.18 | 64.86 | 2.58 | 4.82 | 17.18 | 21.39 | 2.60 | 4.84 |
| 32K | 1 | 4.29 | 16.31 | 0.59 | 1.14 | 4.29 | 5.29 | 0.60 | 1.15 |
| 32K | 8 | 34.36 | 130.49 | 4.74 | 9.13 | 34.36 | 42.36 | 4.78 | 9.17 |
| 64K | 1 | 8.59 | 32.72 | 1.13 | 2.22 | 8.59 | 10.54 | 1.14 | 2.23 |
| 64K | 8 | 68.72 | 261.76 | 9.07 | 17.76 | 68.72 | 84.30 | 9.14 | 17.82 |
| 128K | 1 | 17.18 | 65.54 | 2.22 | 4.38 | 17.18 | 21.02 | 2.23 | 4.39 |
| 128K | 8 | 137.44 | 524.29 | 17.73 | 35.00 | 137.44 | 168.19 | 17.86 | 35.14 |

Stored ratio vs the full fp16 cache is batch-independent: r64 0.151 / 0.139 / 0.133 / 0.130× and
r128 0.282 / 0.267 / 0.259 / 0.256× at 16K / 32K / 64K / 128K (fp16-equivalent: r64 0.086 / 0.075 /
0.070 / 0.067×). The A100 roofline `max(FLOPs/peak, bytes/BW)` with weights included gives ms/token
— full / recon / (ii) / (iii) r64 / (iii) r128 — of 13.1 / 20.8 / 10.7 / 10.7 / 11.1 at 32K batch 1;
32.4 / 94.2 / 14.6 / 13.4 / 16.2 at 32K batch 8; 54.5 / 178.7 / 28.9 / 16.2 / 29.5 at 64K batch 8;
and 98.7 / 347.5 / 57.5 / 30.6 / 58.8 at 128K batch 8 — a lower bound counting tensor passes, not
framework overhead: measured/model at batch 1 is 2.2 / 2.1 / 2.3× for full KV and 6.6 / 9.0 / 16.2×
for the reconstruct path at 16K / 32K / 64K, the excess being per-step re-assembly allocation, GQA
expansion and fp32 elementwise RoPE passes — all of which the kernel removes.

SRAM per program for (iii), blocked **one KV head × M tokens** (bf16 U and C, cos/sin in-kernel):
U_k,U_v head slices `2·D·r·2` B resident across the tile loop, C tiles streamed, K̂/V̂ tiles
materialized.

| r | M | per-program SRAM | A100 164 KB/SM | H100 228 KB/SM |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 32 | 59 KB | 2 blocks | 3 blocks |
| 64 | 64 | 84 KB | 1 block | 2 blocks |
| 64 | 128 | 132 KB | 1 block | 1 block |
| 128 | 32 | 99 KB | 1 block | 2 blocks |
| 128 | 64 | 132 KB | 1 block | 1 block |
| 128 | 128 | 196 KB | does not fit | 1 block |

The whole-n basis does **not** fit: U_k alone is n×r bf16 = 128 KB at r=64, 256 KB at r=128, and
U_k+U_v is 256 / 512 KB against 164 KB (A100) and 228 KB (H100), so per-KV-head blocking is forced,
not chosen — only the D×r slices stay resident, only C tiles stream, and r=64 with M=32 is the one
configuration reaching 2 blocks/SM on A100.

**Accuracy risk.** (i) gives up the pre-RoPE operating point, which "roughly halv[es] the
reconstruction error at matched rank" (`paper/main.tex` §2.2), so it must be tested as *post-RoPE
r=128 vs pre-RoPE r=64* — and even a pass costs 2× the coordinate bytes (0.267× vs 0.139× stored at
32K), failing Gate 3's 0.25× criterion where r=64 passes. Subtler: the surprise score admitting
tokens to the exact tier is computed against the tracked basis, so a post-RoPE basis changes what
reads as surprising — retrieval, not just perplexity, must be re-measured. (ii) and (iii) keep the
shipped basis.

## 4. Decision

**(iii) is primary.** It preserves the shipped pre-RoPE design exactly, moves the same bytes as (i)
and (ii), and is the only option whose extra cost is FLOPs — which this regime mostly gives away. It
meets the Week-3 gate in principle with margin: resident KV 0.60 GB vs full KV's 4.29 GB at 32K, and
a 10.7 ms model floor against the reconstruct path's *measured* 188 ms, so ≥ 3× survives even at a
fifth of that floor. At the Gate-3 point (64K, batch 8) the model gives 16.2 ms and 9.14 GB against
full KV's 54.5 ms and 68.72 GB.

**(i) runs in parallel as an accuracy experiment only** — config `isvd_postrope_r128`, one
Gate-1-style row on Llama 16K, n = 24. It is not a kernel fallback: at the rank it needs for parity
it moves the same bytes as (iii) at r=64 and stores twice as many, so winning buys a simpler kernel,
not a better operating point; it is insurance if (iii) misses its FLOP target on some GPU.

**(ii) is rejected, reason recorded:** under GQA 4:1 it costs exactly G = 4× (iii) on the key side
(532 vs 282 kFLOP/token), moves identical bytes, has worse SRAM pressure and a poor tensor-core
shape. Revisit only for MHA or a wide-head-count model, where G = 1.

**FLOP-bound vs bandwidth-bound crossover for (iii).** KV-side arithmetic intensity is
`(4nr+3n+4·H_q·D)/(2·r·b_C+4) ≈ 2n/b_C` = 546 FLOP/B at r=64 with fp32 coordinates, vs machine
balance 201 (A100) and 296 (H100): the reconstruction is always compute-dense relative to its own
traffic, so what it competes with is the 16.06 GB weight read. Solving `L·φ·x/(P·eff) = W/BW +
L·ψ·x/BW` for `x = B·T_mid`:

| r | A100 @peak | A100 @50 % | H100 @peak | H100 @50 % |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 566 k | 219 k | 1,149 k | 361 k |
| 128 | 298 k | 114 k | 618 k | 189 k |

Below the threshold the step is weight-bandwidth-bound and the reconstruction is free; above it the
kernel is compute-bound. At r=64 on A100 that is batch 8 above ~70K context at peak, or ~27K at the
40–60 % of peak a K = r GEMM realistically attains, so **the 64K/batch-8 Gate-3 cell sits near the
crossover on A100 and well below it on H100** (bandwidth-bound to ~143K at batch 8). Below ~30 %,
r=128 turns compute-bound at batch 8 from 32K up and (i) is the escape hatch. Storing coordinates
bf16 (plan §3.3) doubles the intensity and lowers the crossover: it buys memory, not time.

## 5. Consequences, risks, measurement

- **RoPE in the tile.** Do not stream a cos/sin table — 67 MB per step at 64K. Pass the model's own
  `inv_freq` (D/2 fp32, already carrying Llama-3.1 rope scaling) and `attention_scaling`, and build
  cos/sin in fp32 in-kernel from the tile's int32 positions; fp32 is required, not preferred, since
  angles reach ~10⁵ rad at 128K. Cost ~3n FLOPs/token, ~1 % of the tile's work.
- **Exact tier, ring and sinks are appended dense tiles** in the same tile loop (307 tokens, bf16,
  post-RoPE) sharing the running softmax; at 0.9 % of a 32K context they are a correctness boundary,
  not a cost.
- **Block-16 absorbs invalidate nothing in the kernel path.** `_absorb_columns` eagerly rotates
  retained coordinates into the new basis (`c_k = rot_k @ c_k`), so exactly one current (U, C) pair
  exists at every step: no basis versioning, no memo to drop. That rotation costs ~1.06 GFLOP and ~66 MB per token amortized at 32K r64 (0.4 % of the kernel's FLOPs, ~0.04 ms), and the absorb
  spikes in the measured table (310 / 428 / 850 ms max) go with the memoized middle.
- **Numerics.** The kernel does `U·C` with bf16 inputs and fp32 accumulate, then fp32 RoPE; today's
  path is fp32 `U·C`, fp32 RoPE, then a bf16 cast — i.e. rounding U and C before the r-term dot
  instead of rounding only the result. Same order (~2⁻⁸ relative), roughly √2 worse. The brief's
  `max |Δ| < 1e-2` vs reconstruct-then-attend is the right tripwire; run it on random tensors
  **and** on dumped 8B KV for one layer, since real U/C are far from uniformly scaled.
- **Batch > 1 is a prerequisite:** `lazy_initialization` raises above batch 1, so a batched cache
  lands before the batch ≥ 4 Gate-3 cell. **And full KV may not fit that cell:** weights + full KV
  is 50.4 GB at 64K batch 4 and 84.8 GB at batch 8: neither fits A100-40GB and batch 8 misses
  H100-80GB, while (iii) r64 is 20.6 / 25.2 GB and fits both. Report "max batch that fits" per plan
  §3.2; where full KV OOMs that *is* the result, and the contrast moves to H100 or the largest batch
  full KV holds.
- **Measurement plan.** Promote `scripts/w20_latency.py` to `kvdlra/eval/latency.py` and add the
  kernel arm, protocol unchanged (one token per forward at true positions, CUDA-synced, p50 after
  warm-up, spikes at > 2× p50). `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated` after a post-prefill reset,
  weights subtracted, for full / reconstruct / kernel / KIVI-2 at 16K / 32K / 64K, batch 1 and 4,
  A100 and H100. Report the `accounting.bug_footprint` footprint beside the measured peak, never
  instead of it.

## 6. Milestones (from `docs/plan/lanes/L4_kernel.md`)

- **Week 2 — correctness.** Decode-only Triton kernel: 64-token tiles from `U @ C_tile` (bf16 in,
  fp32 accumulate), RoPE at true positions, fused QKᵀ/softmax/PV, tier + ring + sinks as appended
  dense tiles. `max |Δ| < 1e-2` in bf16 vs reconstruct-then-attend on random and on dumped 8B KV,
  one layer.
- **Week 3 — full model, first numbers.** Greedy decode token-exact on ≥ 14/16 prompts, mismatches
  logged. To beat: **KV peak < 4.08 GB at 32K** (full KV; model 0.60 GB) and **ms/token ≤ 62.8 at
  32K** (188.3 ÷ 3; model floor 10.7 ms).
- **Week 5 — Gate 3.** Resident KV ≤ 0.25× full at 32K (model 0.139× at r=64, 0.267× at r=128 — r=64
  passes, r=128 does not) and tokens/s ≥ full KV at 64K, batch ≥ 4 (model 16.2 vs 54.5 ms at batch
  8, near the A100 crossover).
- **Parallel.** `isvd_postrope_r128`: one Gate-1-style row, Llama 16K, n = 24.

**Status: OPEN until accepted in `docs/plan/DECISIONS.md` (D-002).**
